key_insight: Variational quantum recurrent neural networks match classical performance overall, with one variant showing higher average capacity on a joint memory–nonlinearity task.
engineering_relevance: Task-driven capacity benchmarks help engineers compare quantum and classical recurrent architectures before selecting models for time series prediction.
method: Benchmark memory and nonlinear processing capacity using a task-driven framework.
Compare variational quantum recurrent architectures with classical recurrent baselines.
Assess how model size and parameter initialization affect performance.
evidence_signal: Evaluation uses two generic benchmark tasks and a synthetic chaotic-system dataset; classical models scale better with memory size over the studied range.
watch_item: Quantum model performance is increasingly sensitive to initialization as model size grows, reducing the likelihood of finding good solutions.
paper_title: Benchmarking memory and nonlinear processing capacity of quantum recurrent neural networks for time series prediction
